root.name: Main
root.description:
# Task

Build a URL shortener web service — a single deployable Python app where users paste a long URL and get a short redirect link back.

## Endpoints

- `POST /shorten` — body `{"url": "..."}`, returns `{"short_url": "http://localhost:8000/abc123", "code": "abc123"}`. If the URL already exists return the existing code.
- `GET /{code}` — HTTP 307 redirect to original URL, increments hit_count atomically. Returns 404 if code not found.
- `GET /links` — returns JSON array of all links: `[{"code", "original_url", "created_at", "hit_count"}]`
- `GET /` — serves `static/index.html`

## Database

PostgreSQL, raw SQL via psycopg2-binary (no ORM).

```sql
CREATE TABLE links (
  id           SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  short_code   VARCHAR(6)  NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  original_url TEXT        NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  hit_count    INTEGER     NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);
```

Migration file: `migrations/001_init.sql`

## Short code generation

Use `secrets.token_urlsafe(4)[:6]` — retry on collision (max 5 attempts).

## Frontend

`static/index.html` — vanilla HTML + JS, no build step:
- Form: text input for URL + Submit button
- On submit: POST /shorten, display the resulting short_url
- Table below showing all links from GET /links (auto-refresh after shorten)

## File structure

```
src/api/
  main.py        # FastAPI app, mounts static/, all routes
  db.py          # get_conn(), execute helpers using DATABASE_URL env var
  shortener.py   # generate_code(), shorten_url(), get_link(), list_links()
  config.py      # reads DATABASE_URL from env
src/static/
  index.html
migrations/
  001_init.sql
tests/
  conftest.py    # creates test DB schema, yields TestClient, teardown
  test_api.py    # tests for all 4 endpoints
```

## Runtime

- `uvicorn src.api.main:app --port 8000`
- Env var: `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/urlshortener`

contract.name: Main
contract.description: URL shortener web service — a single deployable Python 3.12 / FastAPI app. Users submit a long URL via POST /shorten and receive a short redirect link. GET /{code} performs a 307 redirect and atomically increments hit_count. GET /links returns all stored links. GET / serves the static HTML frontend. Database is PostgreSQL via psycopg2-binary with raw parameterised SQL. Composed of four modules: config.py (env config), db.py (connection + query helpers), shortener.py (business logic), main.py (FastAPI routes and lifecycle).

functions.name: config.get_config
functions.description: Returns the application configuration singleton. Reads DATABASE_URL from environment on first call, caches the result for subsequent calls. Raises RuntimeError if DATABASE_URL is not set or is empty.

error_cases.name: missing_database_url
error_cases.condition: DATABASE_URL environment variable is not set or is empty string.

error_data.message: DATABASE_URL environment variable is required but not set.

preconditions: Environment variable DATABASE_URL must be set and non-empty.
postconditions: Returned AppConfig.database_url matches the value of os.environ['DATABASE_URL'].
Subsequent calls return the same cached AppConfig instance (singleton).

structured_side_effects.description: Pure read from os.environ, cached after first call. No mutations.

functions.name: db.get_conn
functions.description: Returns a psycopg2 connection to PostgreSQL. Lazily initialises the connection on first call using config.get_config().database_url. Returns the existing connection on subsequent calls. Connection has autocommit=True.

error_cases.name: connection_failed
error_cases.condition: PostgreSQL is unreachable or credentials are invalid.

error_data.message: Could not connect to PostgreSQL at the configured DATABASE_URL.

error_cases.name: config_missing
error_cases.condition: DATABASE_URL not set, propagated from config.get_config().

error_data.message: DATABASE_URL environment variable is required but not set.

preconditions: PostgreSQL server must be reachable at the configured URL.
postconditions: Returned connection is open and usable for queries.
Connection has autocommit=True.

structured_side_effects.description: Opens a TCP connection to PostgreSQL on first call. Subsequent calls return the cached connection.

functions.name: db.execute
functions.description: Executes a parameterised SQL query and returns all result rows as a list of dicts (via RealDictCursor). Returns an empty list for statements with no result set (INSERT without RETURNING, etc.).

inputs.name: query
inputs.description: SQL query string with %s-style parameterised placeholders.

inputs.name: params
inputs.description: Tuple of parameter values to bind to query placeholders.

error_cases.name: query_error
error_cases.condition: SQL syntax error or constraint violation.

error_data.message: Database connection lost during query execution.

preconditions: db.get_conn() has been called or will be called internally.
query uses %s placeholders — no string interpolation.
postconditions: All returned dicts have keys matching the SELECT column names.
For non-SELECT statements, returns empty list.

structured_side_effects.description: Sends SQL query over the database connection and reads the result set.

performance_budget.complexity: O(n) where n is result set size

error_data.message: Database connection lost during query execution.

functions.name: db.close_conn
functions.description: Closes the cached PostgreSQL connection if one is open. Safe to call multiple times. Used during application shutdown.
postconditions: Any cached connection is closed and the module-level reference is reset to None.
Subsequent calls to get_conn() will open a fresh connection.

structured_side_effects.description: Sends connection termination to PostgreSQL if a connection was open.

functions.name: shortener.generate_code
functions.description: Generates a 6-character URL-safe short code using secrets.token_urlsafe(4)[:6]. This is a pure function with no side effects — collision detection is handled by the caller (shorten_url).
postconditions: Returned string is exactly 6 characters.
Returned string matches [A-Za-z0-9_-]{6}.

structured_side_effects.description: Pure function — reads from system CSPRNG via secrets module, no persistent side effects.

functions.name: shortener.shorten_url
functions.description: Shortens a URL. If the original_url already exists in the links table, returns the existing code (idempotent). Otherwise generates a new short code, inserts the row, and returns the ShortenResponse. Retries up to 5 times on short_code collision (UNIQUE constraint violation).

inputs.name: original_url
inputs.description: The long URL to shorten. Must be a valid HTTP/HTTPS URL.

validators.error_message: URL must be a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL.

error_cases.name: code_collision_exhausted
error_cases.condition: All 5 retry attempts produced short codes that collide with existing codes.

error_data.message: Failed to generate a unique short code after 5 attempts.

error_cases.name: database_error
error_cases.condition: Unexpected database error during INSERT or SELECT.

preconditions: The links table exists with the expected schema.
postconditions: A row with the given original_url exists in the links table.
Returned ShortenResponse.code corresponds to the row's short_code.
Returned ShortenResponse.short_url is http://localhost:8000/{code}.
If the URL already existed, no new row was inserted and the existing code is returned.

structured_side_effects.description: SELECT to check for existing URL, INSERT to create new link row. Up to 5 INSERT retries on collision.

functions.name: shortener.resolve_and_track
functions.description: Resolves a short code to its original URL and atomically increments hit_count. Uses a single UPDATE links SET hit_count = hit_count + 1 WHERE short_code = %s RETURNING original_url query for atomicity.

validators.error_message: Code must be exactly 6 URL-safe characters.

preconditions: The links table exists with the expected schema.
postconditions: If a row with matching short_code exists: hit_count is incremented by exactly 1, and original_url is returned.
If no row matches: None is returned and no rows are modified.

structured_side_effects.description: Atomically increments hit_count by 1 for the matching short_code row via UPDATE...RETURNING.

performance_budget.complexity: O(1) — single indexed UPDATE by UNIQUE short_code

functions.name: shortener.list_links
functions.description: Returns all link records from the links table, ordered by created_at descending (newest first). Maps each row dict to a LinkListItem.
preconditions: The links table exists with the expected schema.
postconditions: Returned list contains one LinkListItem per row in the links table.
List is ordered by created_at descending.
Each LinkListItem.hit_count reflects the current database value.

structured_side_effects.description: SELECT all rows from links ordered by created_at DESC.

performance_budget.complexity: O(n) where n is the number of links in the table

inputs.name: code

validators.error_message: Code must be exactly 6 URL-safe characters.

functions.name: main.startup_event
functions.description: FastAPI startup lifecycle event handler. Verifies the database connection is viable by calling db.get_conn(). Logs a message on success. If the connection fails, the error propagates and prevents uvicorn from accepting requests.

error_cases.name: db_unreachable
error_cases.condition: PostgreSQL is not reachable at startup.

error_data.message: Cannot connect to PostgreSQL. Application startup aborted.
DATABASE_URL environment variable is required but not set.

postconditions: A database connection has been established and cached in db module.
Application is ready to accept HTTP requests.

structured_side_effects.description: Establishes initial database connection to verify connectivity at startup.
Logs a startup message confirming database connectivity.

functions.name: main.shutdown_event
functions.description: FastAPI shutdown lifecycle event handler. Calls db.close_conn() to cleanly close the PostgreSQL connection.
postconditions: Database connection is closed.
Module-level connection reference in db.py is reset to None.

structured_side_effects.description: Logs a shutdown message confirming connection closure.

invariants: All SQL queries use parameterised placeholders ($1, %s) — never string interpolation or f-strings.
Short codes are exactly 6 URL-safe characters matching the regex [A-Za-z0-9_-]{6}.
The original_url column has a UNIQUE constraint; submitting the same URL always returns the existing code (idempotent).
The short_code column has a UNIQUE constraint; collisions are retried up to 5 times before raising CodeCollisionError.
hit_count is incremented atomically via UPDATE ... SET hit_count = hit_count + 1 RETURNING original_url.
DATABASE_URL must be a valid PostgreSQL connection string or the app refuses to start.
Route definition order in main.py: GET /, GET /links, GET /{code}, POST /shorten — to prevent path parameter from capturing literal paths.
No ORM or SQLAlchemy — only raw SQL via psycopg2-binary.
Each source file is under 200 lines.

data_access.rationale: Reads DATABASE_URL from environment (INTERNAL configuration secret). Reads and writes the 'links' table in PostgreSQL which contains user-submitted URLs (PUBLIC), short codes (PUBLIC), timestamps (PUBLIC), and hit counts (PUBLIC). The database connection string is classified INTERNAL because it contains credentials. All link data is PUBLIC — no PII is collected.

side_effects.rationale: Reads database connection string from environment variables at startup to establish PostgreSQL connection.
Queries the links table to resolve short codes to original URLs and to list all stored links.
Inserts new link rows when shortening URLs and atomically increments hit_count on each redirect.
Serves the static HTML frontend file from disk on GET / requests.

authority.rationale: This component is the sole owner of the 'links' table in PostgreSQL, which stores all short-code-to-URL mappings. It is the authoritative source for short code generation, URL-to-code resolution, and hit_count tracking. No other component reads or writes the links domain.
